Front: four square post locations are consistent with tray corners; upper and lower thick shallow tray lips join the frame. Front wheel pair contacts the floor and rear casters are normally occluded. Tote sits inside the upper tray; handle is behind it.

Side: two distinct tray levels, square support posts, grounded caster assemblies and raised rear handle remain connected. Same tote and tray structure as front/rear; no third shelf, detached wheel or floating rail.
Rear: the two rear posts rise to one broad connected push bar. Lower tray remains open/empty; tote is supported inside the upper tray, and rear casters join the frame.

Three-quarter: tangible floor/lip thickness, square posts, under-tray air space and three visible grounded casters with the fourth normally hidden. Tote is separate, hollow and supported; the tray does not become a closed box.

Top fit inset shows a continuous visible tan clearance border around the centered petrol tote. All four sides of its base remain within the tray. Printed dimensions are concept targets, not measured outer-base validation.

Worker grip inset: one friendly cuboid blue picker, charcoal sleeves/navy trousers/charcoal boots and trolley01 badge; both mitten hands visibly contact the broad handle, elbows naturally bent and feet grounded. No hand holds the tote simultaneously.

Compared against actually viewed R01/R04/R05: matte petrol/charcoal/tan structure, thick open R04-like tote and blue cuboid picker language remain consistent. R05 remains the authority for detailed worker construction; this small inset specifies grip interaction.

No significant reference defect found in the first iteration. Later geometry must verify outer tote footprint, tray usable opening, all four wheel contacts, exact handle reach/pivots and loaded movement; image pixels do not establish engineering dimensions.
